concepts.title: Latitude, Longitude and Their Grid
concepts.definition: Latitude is the angular distance north or south of the equator measured in degrees up to 90, longitude is the angular distance east or west of the Prime Meridian at Greenwich up to 180, and the grid of parallels and meridians fixes every place on the earth.
concepts.key_idea: Parallels stay equally spaced while meridians converge at the poles, and one degree of latitude always spans about 111 km.

concepts.title: Time Difference, International Date Line and Standard Time
concepts.definition: The earth rotates 360 degrees in 24 hours, so one degree of longitude equals four minutes of time, and places east of Greenwich are ahead while places west are behind; the International Date Line near the 180 degree meridian changes the date when crossed, and countries adopt standard time zones of their chosen meridians.
concepts.key_idea: The time lag between two places equals their longitude difference in degrees multiplied by four minutes, and India's single IST spans about 30 degrees of longitude.

concepts.title: Meridians, Zones and the Grid Reference System
concepts.definition: The grid of parallels and meridians divides the globe into time and position zones, and on maps the grid reference of eastings and northings pinpoints any location to six figures, linking the spherical coordinate system to practical map reading.
concepts.key_idea: A six figure grid reference gives easting first and northing second, locating a point within 100 metres on a 1:50,000 sheet.
